newsitem.title: USA: Highlands lowers price for Vik Brothers Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Highlands lowers price for Vik Brothers Insurance.

text.p: Highlands Insurance Group Inc. said Friday it has again reduced the price it will pay to acquire Vik Brothers Insurance Inc. of Lawrenceville, N.J., to about $97 million.

In January, the companies agreed to lower the price to $110 million from the $164 million originally agreed upon in June 1996, after Vik lost $8.9 million for the nine months ended Sept. 30 due to major catastrophe losses.
Highlands, a Houston-based company that specialises in commercial property and casualty insurance, did not specify the reason for the latest price cut.
The price includes the assumption of debt.
Highlands said it will finance the acquisition with a combination of common stock, bank debt and preferred stock.
Highlands will issue about 1.7 million common shares, which would comprise about 13 percent of its outstanding stock.
The parties expect to close the deal by April 30, Highlands said.
Highland's stock rose 12.5 cents to $22.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
